findings.title: Landing regression omits actual remote-head verification
findings.why_it_matters: The test verifies local HEAD against origin/<branch>, but never queries the actual remote. It cannot catch the newly specified failure where local HEAD and a stale tracking ref agree while the published branch differs. Removing the actual-remote requirement from the wrapper would leave this test green.
findings.suggested_fix: Query the bare remote with git ls-remote, assert local/tracking/remote agreement, and advance the remote through a second checkout without refreshing the first tracking ref to prove matching local/tracking heads are insufficient. Retain a focused actual-remote wrapper-contract assertion.
evidence: Lines 110-113 compare only HEAD with origin/<branch> after pushing.
Lines 118-120 assert porcelain, unpushed and failure-banner wording, not actual-remote verification.
The changed source land wrapper requires actual remote verification because a stale tracking ref is not publication evidence.

findings.title: Untracked-subject test never proves staging restores coverage
findings.why_it_matters: The asserted CE file list was captured before the untracked file existed, so absence from that cached list is guaranteed. The test discovers the CLI subject but does not verify staging and re-enumeration restores coverage for either lane.
findings.suggested_fix: Check the CLI exit code, recompute pinned Git diff after creating the subject, assert missing subset coverage, deliberately stage it, rerun both enumerations, and assert unchanged base and restored subset coverage in both lanes.
